name: Annual mineral resource and reserve estimate
summary: Once a year a listed mining company must say how much gold it has in the ground (resources) and how much it can mine at a profit (reserves). Mine geologists rebuild the geological model with the year's drilling, independent consultants estimate grades, the engineers apply stope shapes, costs, dilution and the gold price, and qualified persons review and sign before the statement is published with the year-end results in March. It is slow because late assays hold up the database freeze, interpretation is a long manual task, the model is reconciled against what the mill actually recovered, and every number must agree across the news release, the annual information form and the financial statements.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer listed on the TSX that uses site geologists and engineers with independent consultant qualified persons.
baseline.notes: One case is one annual estimate, from setting the data cut-off in early autumn to publication in March.

unit_of_work: one annual mineral resource and reserve estimate
trigger: The annual estimate cycle starts in early autumn so that the statement, effective 31 December, can be published with year-end results.
end_state: The resource and reserve statement is published and the model and tables are issued to planning and disclosure.

volume.seasonality: Work runs from September or October to March every year.

evidence.note: Annual updates effective 31 December, published in March.
Plans the estimate, reviews interpretation and reconciliation, drafts the statement.
Database freeze, validation and wireframe update take about 200 hours a year across the geology team.
Cut-off, reserve stope design, schedule and tabulation take about 200 hours a year.
Supplies mined-out solids for depletion; not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Engages consultants and approves the estimate.
Company qualified person for technical disclosure.
Approves metal price and exchange rate assumptions; not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Disclosure review of the statement and news release text; not listed for this process in the organisation file.

roles.title: Independent resource and reserve consultant (qualified person)

evidence.note: Independent consultants estimated the reference mine's resources and reserves under company supervision. Billing rate is the author's estimate for senior Canadian geological and mining consultants.

systems.name: Mine design and scheduling software (3D design, scheduling)
Total stations, cavity monitoring scanner and survey software
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)

steps.name: Set the data cut-off and timetable
steps.description: The chief geologist sets the date after which new drill results will wait for next year, agrees the timetable back from the March results release with the technical services manager and engineering, and lists which zones need a full remodel. He sends the plan to the team and consultants.

error.defect_description: Cut-off set before key drill results return, leaving them out.

evidence.note: Recent drilling was to be included in the annual update published in March.

steps.name: Engage the independent consultants
steps.description: The technical services manager confirms scope, fees and dates with the resource and reserve consultants and raises the purchase order. He sends them the timetable and the access they need to the database and models.

error.defect_description: Scope omits a zone that then has to be added late.

evidence.note: Independent consultants under company supervision prepared the reference estimates.

steps.name: Wait for outstanding assays and freeze the database
steps.description: The mine geologist chases the commercial laboratory and site lab for assays from holes drilled before the cut-off, loads the last certificates, then exports a frozen copy of collars, surveys, logs and assays for the estimate. Late assays are the usual reason the freeze slips.

error.defect_description: Certificate loaded against the wrong hole or interval.

evidence.note: Definition core is assayed at an outside commercial laboratory at a comparable mine; turnaround is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Validate the database and QA/QC
steps.description: The geologist checks collars against survey, downhole surveys for jumps, overlapping or missing intervals, and assays against the certificates, and reviews standards, blanks and duplicates for failures. Failed batches go back to the lab for re-assay.

error.defect_description: A swapped sample is not detected.

evidence.note: Standards and blanks each at 1 in 25 samples and check pulps at a second lab at a comparable mine.

steps.name: Update the geological interpretation
steps.description: The geologist updates the vein and zone wireframes with the year's drill holes and face mapping, splits domains where grade behaviour differs, and builds the mined-out and development solids into the model. This is the longest single task in the estimate.

error.defect_description: A vein is extended past the drilling support, adding tonnes.

evidence.note: Comparable mine builds block models by domain from wireframed zones.

steps.name: Chief geologist reviews the interpretation
steps.description: The chief geologist reviews the wireframes section by section against the drill holes and underground mapping and asks for changes where continuity is stretched. About one interpretation in five goes back.

error.defect_description: Overextended zone passes review.

evidence.note: Internal peer review of interpretation is common practice; the wait reflects the chief geologist's rotation.

steps.name: Compile depletion solids to year end
steps.description: The surveyor compiles the cavity scans of mined stopes and the as-built development to date and adds the planned mining to 31 December, so the model can be depleted to the effective date. He sends the solids to geology and engineering.

error.defect_description: A stope mined late in the year is not depleted.

evidence.note: Depletion to the effective date is standard practice.

steps.name: Composite, cap and analyse grades
steps.description: The resource consultant composites assays to a fixed length within each domain, studies grade distributions to choose capping levels, and models spatial continuity to set search ranges. He documents the parameters in a memo.

error.defect_description: Capping level too high for a high-grade domain.

evidence.note: Capping by zone and composite-based capping at comparable mines.

steps.name: Estimate block model grades
steps.description: The consultant builds the block model, interpolates gold grades by ordinary kriging or inverse distance with several search passes, assigns density and flags the depleted blocks. He runs the model for every domain that changed.

error.defect_description: Search too wide in sparse areas smooths grade.

evidence.note: Ordinary kriging and ID2 with three search passes at a comparable mine.

steps.name: Validate the block model
steps.description: The consultant checks the model against the composites with swath plots, a nearest-neighbour comparison and visual sections, and fixes blocks that look wrong. He sends the model with a validation memo to the chief geologist.

error.defect_description: Local bias in one domain not visible on swath plots.

evidence.note: Validation with nearest neighbour, ID3 and Snowden Supervisor at a comparable mine.

steps.name: Reconcile the model to production
steps.description: The chief geologist compares the model's tonnes, grade and ounces for the stopes mined this year with the grade control model and the mill's reconciled ounces. When the model is well off, he sends it back with changes to capping or search.

error.defect_description: Reconciliation period chosen to flatter the model.

evidence.note: Comparable mine reconciled block models to mill head ounces and revised capping after the model ran 7 percent low.

steps.name: Classify and report mineral resources
steps.description: The consultant classifies blocks as measured, indicated or inferred from drill spacing and confidence, applies stope shapes to show reasonable prospects of economic extraction at the resource cut-off, and tabulates the resource. He writes the resource notes.

error.defect_description: Isolated blocks classified indicated without enough drilling.

evidence.note: CIM standards and a separate resource cut-off at the reference company.

steps.name: Approve metal price and exchange rate
steps.description: The chief operating officer and chief financial officer set the reserve and resource gold prices and the exchange rate, usually below spot and consistent with peers, and send them to site. Engineering cannot finish cut-offs until they arrive.

error.defect_description: Price deck differs from the budget's assumptions without explanation.

control.basis: Company policy on long-term metal price assumptions for disclosure

evidence.note: Separate reserve and resource prices (US$1,400 and US$1,500) and exchange rate at the reference company.

steps.name: Calculate cut-off grades
steps.description: The planning engineer takes mining, milling and general costs per tonne from the year's cost reports, the approved price, mill recovery and royalties, and calculates the reserve and resource cut-off grades and the incremental cut-off for development ore.

error.defect_description: Cost per tonne taken from a period with abnormal costs.

evidence.note: Cut-offs built from costs per tonne, price and recovery at the reference and comparable mines.

steps.name: Design reserve stopes and apply modifying factors
steps.description: The engineer runs stope shapes on the measured and indicated blocks at the reserve cut-off, adds the development to reach them, and applies wall dilution, minimum mining width and mining recovery. He removes stopes that do not pay for their own access.

error.defect_description: Dilution applied inconsistently between zones.

evidence.note: 1.5 m minimum width, 0.5 m dilution per wall and 90 percent mine recovery at the reference mine.

steps.name: Schedule and test reserve economics
steps.description: The engineer schedules the reserve stopes and development at achievable rates and runs a cash flow at the reserve price to show that the reserve as a whole is economic. Blocks that fail are removed and the schedule rerun.

error.defect_description: Schedule assumes development rates above actuals.

evidence.note: Comparable report supports reserves with a life-of-mine schedule and cash flow.

steps.name: Tabulate reserves and explain changes
steps.description: The engineer tabulates proven and probable reserves by zone and builds the year-on-year bridge: depletion by mining, additions from drilling, model changes and price or cost changes. He checks the totals against the resource model.

error.defect_description: Depletion double-counted in the bridge.

evidence.note: Year-on-year reconciliation of reserves is normal disclosure practice.

steps.name: Independent qualified person reviews the reserve
steps.description: The reserve consultant reviews the cut-offs, stope shapes, modifying factors, schedule and tabulation, visits site if he has not recently, and lists issues. About one estimate in seven needs rework of stope design or factors.

error.defect_description: Review relies on company data without independent checks.

control.basis: National Instrument 43-101: scientific and technical disclosure based on information prepared by or under the supervision of a qualified person

evidence.note: Independent consultant as reserve QP at the reference company; CIM best practice guidance (2019 version adopted November 2019) on the QP's role.

steps.name: Technical services manager approves the estimate
steps.description: The technical services manager reviews the final tables, the change bridge and the consultants' comments and approves the estimate for the company. He confirms the reserve is consistent with the mine plan the site is working to.

error.defect_description: Inconsistency with the LOM plan missed.

evidence.note: Site approval step from general practice.

steps.name: Company qualified person signs off
steps.description: The vice-president exploration, as the company's qualified person, reviews the estimate and the notes for disclosure and accepts it. Questions go back to site by email and call.

error.defect_description: Accepted without reconciling to prior statement.

control.basis: National Instrument 43-101: scientific and technical disclosure based on information prepared by or under the supervision of a qualified person

evidence.note: Reference company names its VP exploration and COO as qualified persons for technical disclosure.

steps.name: Draft the statement tables and notes
steps.description: The chief geologist drafts the resource and reserve tables and the notes on cut-off, price, dilution, recovery, density and the qualified persons, in the format of the prior year's release, and writes a short explanation of the changes.

error.defect_description: Rounding or note mismatch between tables and text.

evidence.note: Reference release format: tables by category with notes on cut-off, price, width, dilution, recovery and density.

steps.name: Legal and disclosure review
steps.description: The general counsel and the chief financial officer check the statement against the news release, the annual information form and the financial statements, and check the qualified person and cautionary language. About one draft in six comes back with changes.

error.defect_description: Inconsistent number left in the AIF draft.

control.basis: National Instrument 43-101 and National Instrument 51-102 continuous disclosure requirements

evidence.note: Disclosure review practice for TSX-listed producers; regulation text not opened.

steps.name: Qualified persons consent to the disclosure
steps.description: The independent consultants read the final text and give written consent to being named and to the summary of their work. A late wording change can send it back to them.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: National Instrument 43-101: scientific and technical disclosure based on information prepared by or under the supervision of a qualified person

evidence.note: Independent QPs named in the reference release.

steps.name: Publish with year-end results and issue to users
steps.description: The statement is released with the year-end results in March and the chief geologist sends the final model, tables and change bridge to engineering for the plan and to head office for the annual information form. The files are archived as the year's estimate of record.

error.defect_description: Superseded model version sent to engineering.

evidence.note: Updates are released in March with year-end results (13 March 2023; March 2021 stated in advance).

exceptions.name: Late or failed assays
exceptions.description: QA/QC failures or missing certificates send batches back to the lab and push the database freeze.

exceptions.name: Model does not reconcile to the mill
exceptions.description: The model's ounces for mined stopes differ from the mill and the consultant revises capping or search.

exceptions.name: Reserve rework after QP review
exceptions.description: The independent QP finds stope design or modifying factor issues and engineering redoes the reserve.

exceptions.name: Disclosure text inconsistent
exceptions.description: Numbers or notes differ between the statement, news release and AIF and the draft is redone.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from data cut-off planning to publication
benchmarks.population: Annual estimate at a single-mine TSX gold producer

evidence.note: Author's estimate: work starts in late September or October and the statement is published in mid-March (src1, src2).

benchmarks.population: Reference company, estimate effective 31 December 2022 published 13 March 2023

pain_points.description: The database freeze waits on late assays from outside labs, which compresses the modelling time before year end.

evidence.note: Comparable report recommends improving assay turnaround.

pain_points.description: Wireframe interpretation and reserve stope design are long manual tasks done by a few people, and review loops repeat them.

evidence.note: Touch times in the steps; general practice.

pain_points.description: Model-to-mill differences force late changes to capping or search after the model was thought finished.

evidence.note: Comparable mine's model ran 4.5-11.5 percent low against mill ounces.

pain_points.description: Every number has to agree across the statement, news release, AIF and financial statements, checked by hand.

evidence.note: Organisation file notes line-by-line consistency checks in disclosure.

assumptions: Loaded costs come from the organisation file; the consultant rate is a billing rate, so the simulated labour cost includes consultant fees.

The workflow follows the reference company's model of independent consultants doing the estimation and reserve work under company supervision; some comparable mines (src3, src4) use site staff as qualified persons, which would move steps s08-s12 and s18 to the chief geologist and chief engineer.
The organisation file lists no trigger for this process; the case is started by the annual calendar, and the year's definition drill results are used as the triggering object.
Surveyor, chief operating officer and general counsel take part but are not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Software names in the comparable report (Datamine, Snowden Supervisor) are examples; the reference mine's software was not confirmed.

Organisation file corrected on 2026-11-24 to match this workflow's sources: ids were renamed (mill-elution-refining to mill-gold-room-refining, loaded_carbon to gold_concentrate, tailings_slurry to filtered_tailings, elution-circuit to refinery), and roles and resources this workflow added are now in the organisation file. Notes above that describe a mismatch refer to the file before the correction.
